skill.name: scope
skill.description: Defines project scope from requirements and research using feature lists, MoSCoW priorities, and relative effort estimates. Compares technology options, requires user approval, and creates a dated SCOPE document without generating code.
skill.summary: Turn requirements and research into an approved project scope and technology stack.
skill.author: cubha

security_audit.summary: All 31 external-command alerts are Markdown formatting or benign command documentation, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The entropy alert reflects Korean and Unicode text, not obfuscation. Two medium semantic risks remain around unrestricted research paths and treating loaded research as trusted instructions.

remediation.issue: The --from option does not explicitly restrict or normalize the supplied file path.
remediation.suggestion: Allow only normalized docs/research/RESEARCH-*.md paths, reject absolute paths and traversal, and require confirmation for any exception.

remediation.issue: Loaded research documents are used without an explicit untrusted-content boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Treat research text as data, ignore embedded instructions, summarize relevant evidence, and request confirmation before acting on unexpected directives.

content.user_title: Define Project Scope and Approve the Stack
content.value_statement: Unclear requirements cause scope creep and premature technology choices. This skill converts requirements and research into prioritized scope, effort estimates, and an approved technology stack.
actual_capabilities: Loads a selected research document or finds RESEARCH files under docs/research.
Asks only for missing details that affect scope or technology decisions.
Breaks requirements into user-value features and assigns MoSCoW priorities.
Estimates Must and Should features with relative T-shirt sizes.
Compares relevant technology categories and requires user approval before finalizing choices.
Creates a dated SCOPE document or returns the same content in the conversation.
limitations: Does not generate application code, configuration, or project scaffolding.
Provides relative effort estimates, not schedules or contractual delivery dates.
Does not perform broad market or technology research.
Produces weaker stack recommendations when no research evidence is available.

use_cases.title: Prioritize an MVP
use_cases.description: Convert product requirements into Must, Should, Could, and Won't features with relative effort.

use_cases.title: Select a Practical Stack
use_cases.description: Compare technology options against required features before committing development resources.

use_cases.title: Create an Engineering Handoff
use_cases.description: Produce an approved scope document that can guide planning and project scaffolding.

prompt_templates.title: Scope a Simple Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Define the scope for [project]. The target user is [user], and the main problem is [problem].
prompt_templates.scenario: Start from a short project idea.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize an MVP
prompt_templates.prompt: Scope an MVP for [project]. Separate features with MoSCoW priorities and estimate Must and Should items with T-shirt sizes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn known requirements into a release boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Use Existing Research
prompt_templates.prompt: Scope [project] using [research file]. Compare only stack categories required by Must features, then ask for approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Base decisions on an existing research document.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Constraints and Risks
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a scope for [project] under [constraints]. Identify uncertain XL items, compare stack tradeoffs, record rejected options, and require approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Make an advanced scope decision with explicit constraints.

output_examples.input: Scope a lightweight appointment booking MVP for one clinic.
output: Must: available time slots, booking, cancellation, and clinic notifications.
Should: reminder messages and basic appointment management.
Won't now: payments, multiple clinics, and insurance processing.
Risk: calendar synchronization needs validation before implementation.

output_examples.input: Compare stacks for a small internal inventory tool and require approval.
output_examples.output: Recommended stack: a browser interface, managed relational database, and company identity provider. Approval is required before the stack enters the SCOPE document.

output_examples.input: Create the scope in conversation without writing a file.
output_examples.output: The response includes the project definition, prioritized features, relative estimates, approved stack, risks, and unresolved decisions.

best_practices: Provide the target user, core problem, deployment constraints, and excluded technologies.
Keep Must features limited to the smallest set that delivers the core value.
Review XL estimates and stack tradeoffs before approving the final document.
anti_patterns: Do not treat every requested feature as a Must requirement.
Do not accept a technology stack without reviewing its fit and tradeoffs.
Do not use relative estimates as guaranteed delivery dates.

faq.question: Does this skill write application code?
faq.answer: No. It creates scope documentation and leaves code generation to later workflows.

faq.question: What does the skill need to begin?
faq.answer: Provide a project idea or requirements. Target users, constraints, and research improve the result.

faq.question: Can it use an existing research document?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide a RESEARCH Markdown file or let the skill search docs/research.

faq.question: How are effort estimates expressed?
faq.answer: Features receive S, M, L, or XL relative sizes. These values show scale and uncertainty.

faq.question: Can I skip technology selection?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the documented skip-stack option to perform scope planning without the approval gate.

faq.question: Will it overwrite an existing SCOPE document?
faq.answer: No. It creates a dated document and keeps existing SCOPE files.
